name: lua-lstrlib
url: https://github.com/lua/lua (git clone --depth 1 of https://github.com/lua/lua.git, checked out at tag v5.4.9 = commit 312b9efaa1061c2c4cad08554dbc1351c3270eef; only files read: lstrlib.c, luaconf.h, llimits.h, lua.h)
files_measured: lua/lstrlib.c only (single TU, compiled with the repo's own headers via -I lua/). Whole TU on Cortex-M4 = text 9641 (data 0, bss 0); the engine number below is the SUM of the pattern-matching functions (lstrlib.c lines 347-669, section 'PATTERN MATCHING') taken from the per-function breakdown, cross-checked with a wrapper TU + 'arm-none-eabi-ld -r --gc-sections -u lua_pat_search' which keeps exactly the same 11 sections (1397 B incl. a 4 B wrapper thunk).
build_cmd_file: $WORK/engines/lua-lstrlib/BUILD.txt (generated by sh $WORK/engines/lua-lstrlib/build.sh; also $WORK/engines/lua-lstrlib/measure_lstrlib_full.txt, classify.py, classify_seed1.txt, difftest_seed1.txt)
per_function_top: Cortex-M4 -Os, engine sections: match 640 (max_expand, min_expand, end_capture, match_capture, matchbalance, check_capture, capture_to_close are all inlined into it - they have no symbol of their own); match_class 176; classend 108; matchbracketclass 88; start_capture 64; singlematch.isra.0 60; rodata error strings: .rodata.match.str1.1 126 ('pattern too complex', 'invalid pattern capture', 'malformed pattern (missing arguments to %b)', 'missing [ after %f'), .rodata.classend.str1.1 67, .rodata.get_onecapture.str1.1 46 ('invalid capture index %%%d' used by inlined check_capture), .rodata.push_captures.str1.1 18 ('too many captures' used by start_capture). Sum: text 1136 + rodata 257 = 1393. For scale, the Lua-API glue in the same file: str_find_aux 396, str_gsub 692, gmatch 120+92, push_captures 60, get_onecapture 88, push_onecapture 32. Cortex-M0+: match 632, match_class 152, classend 100, matchbracketclass 88, start_capture 64, singlematch 58 = 1094 + 257 rodata = 1351. x86-64 (clang, sizes from nm -n address deltas because Mach-O has no symbol sizes): match 1112, match_class 582 (macOS ctype inlined), classend 158, matchbracketclass 155, start_capture 118, singlematch 75 = 2200 + 257 cstrings = 2457.
excluded_functions: Everything outside lines 347-669: str_find_aux (search loop + captures push), str_find, str_match, gmatch, gmatch_aux, str_gsub, add_s, add_value, push_captures, push_onecapture, get_onecapture, lmemfind, nospecials, prepstate/reprepstate (MatchState init; inlined into the glue, ~10 instructions), plus the unrelated string library (str_format 1376, str_pack 712, str_unpack 408, getoption 500, str_rep, str_byte, arith*, luaopen_string, strlib/stringmetamethods tables ...). No test/debug code exists in the file. The two shared error strings (46+18 B) are INCLUDED because the matcher's own inlined check_capture/start_capture reference them (relocations verified with objdump -dr; see BUILD.txt 'RELOCS').
libc_deps: For the six matcher sections specifically (objdump -dr relocations, BUILD.txt): luaL_error (Lua aux lib; the ONLY error path - it longjmps through the lua_State, the matcher has no error return value), memcmp (match_capture / %1 back-references), _ctype_ (newlib ctype table, 257 B in libc.a of GNU Arm Embedded 10.3-2021.10, via isalpha/isdigit/isspace/isalnum/... and tolower/islower in match_class). No malloc, no strlen, no setjmp inside the matcher itself (setjmp/longjmp live in luaL_error->lua_error->luaD_throw). Whole-TU nm -u additionally lists ~55 lua_*/luaL_* symbols, memchr, memcpy, snprintf, strchr, strcpy, strlen, strpbrk, strspn, localeconv, __aeabi_* float helpers - all from the non-matcher string functions.
ram_model: No malloc. MatchState is a caller-stack struct: sizeof = 280 B on ARM (3 ptrs + lua_State* + int matchdepth + uchar level + 32 x {ptr,ptrdiff_t} capture slots = 8 B each; LUA_MAXCAPTURES=32 at lstrlib.c:35). Backtracking is by C recursion: match() frame 40 B, start_capture 24 B (-fstack-usage, M4). Depth grows with the number of quantified items ('*' '+' '?' '-') and '(' ')' in the PATTERN, not with the text (plain items, %b, %f, %n use 'goto init'); max_expand counts repetitions iteratively then retries backwards (no per-repetition recursion). Hard cap MAXCCALLS=200 nested match() calls ('pattern too complex' error, lstrlib.c:378) => worst case ~200*(40+24) = ~13 KB stack; typical short patterns use well under 1 KB. Captures are (pointer,len) pairs into the subject string; no copy.
features_verified: Read from lstrlib.c lines 347-669 and probed via the driver's raw mode (LUAPAT_RAW=1 passes native Lua syntax; results in BUILD.txt/this session): literal bytes; '.' = any BYTE incl. newline; '^' anchor only as first pattern char (handled by the caller's search loop, str_find_aux, not by match()); '$' only as last pattern char, matches only at the very end (not before a trailing newline); single-char classes %a %c %d %g %l %p %s %u %w %x %z (deprecated NUL) and their uppercase complements, all ctype-based = ASCII in the C locale; '%' + non-alphanumeric = literal escape; [set] with ranges a-z, %classes inside, [^set] negation, ']' as first member; quantifiers ONLY on a single-char item: * (greedy), + (greedy), - (lazy zero-or-more), ? (greedy optional); captures ( ) up to 32 with byte offsets, position captures '()', back-references %1-%9 (byte-exact memcmp), %bxy balanced match, %f[set] frontier (a generalised word boundary). NOT implemented: alternation '|' (no such construct at all), counted {n,m}, quantifiers on groups (x)*, lazy '+?' / '??' (only the '-' lazy star exists; 'x+?' is expressible as 'xx-'), non-capturing groups, any case-insensitive flag (no code for it), UTF-8 awareness (pure bytes; a 2-byte literal followed by '*' quantifies only its last byte), \d \w \s spelling, \b, \xHH, lookaround, no compile step / no pattern validation up front (errors are raised lazily during matching). Verified via corpus (809 passes): literals, classes/ranges/negation, \d\w\s via %d/[%w_]/%s translation, greedy * + ?, lazy *? and +? (via '-'), captures (groups checked correct in 10 of the 14 group-span checks the runner performed), ^ and $, ASCII case-insensitivity ONLY through the driver expanding letters to [aA] sets (84/212 -i cases pass; the engine itself has no -i).
difftest: Driver: $WORK/engines/lua-lstrlib/driver.c (186 lines, NOT ~40: Lua patterns are a different language, so the driver does a purely syntactic regex->Lua-pattern translation (\d->%d, \w->[%w_], [..]->[..] with %-escaping, a*?->a-, a+?->aa-, -i -> [aA] sets, (?:..) dropped, ^/$ only at pattern ends) and prints 'error unsupported:<feature>' for constructs Lua patterns cannot express; the search-anywhere loop is a copy of str_find_aux; captures come from MatchState). Result on corpus_seed1.jsonl (python3 difftest.py, full line in BUILD.txt): cases=2088 checked=2081 pass=809 fail=1272 timeouts=0 group_spans_checked=14. Classification of the 1272 failures (classify.py, first unsupported construct hit wins, so a pattern with both '|' and '{n}' counts once): MISSING FEATURE 1211 = alternation '|' 582, counted {n,m} 408, quantified group 139, lazy '??' 82 (\b word boundary appears in 4 corpus patterns but was always preceded by another unsupported construct). SEMANTICS DIFFERENCE 61 = byte-wise UTF-8 matching 59 ('.'/[^..]/\W consume one byte: '.' on 'é' gives [0,1] not [0,2]; a quantified multi-byte literal 'é+' repeats only its last byte), '.' matching newline 2. BUGS 0, ENGINE ERRORS 0 ('pattern too complex' never triggered), TIMEOUTS 0. The 7 corpus cases Python rejects are skipped by the runner. Everything Lua patterns CAN express passed, i.e. no wrong answers were found for the shared feature subset.
caveats: (1) The 1393 B is the matcher WITHOUT its host: it cannot run standalone - it needs a lua_State pointer for luaL_error (longjmp error reporting), plus newlib's 257 B _ctype_ table, memcmp, and a caller that provides the search loop (~30 instructions of str_find_aux) and the 280 B MatchState. A faithful standalone port would be ~1.5-1.7 KB incl. a longjmp/flag-based error stub. (2) It is NOT a regex engine: no alternation, no {n,m}, no group quantifiers, no lazy +?/??, no -i, byte-only; it fails 61% of the corpus, 95% of those for missing syntax. The size is therefore a lower bound comparable, not a competitor. (3) Backtracking is recursive C (bounded by MAXCCALLS=200 => 'pattern too complex' error rather than stack overflow). (4) -i in the difftest is emulated by the driver ([aA] sets), not by the engine; back-references under -i would be case-sensitive (0 such cases reached the engine). (5) The clone is tag v5.4.9 from the GitHub mirror (the official source is lua.org tarballs; the repo carries no manual, so feature claims come from reading lstrlib.c, not docs). (6) The 'lua/lstrlib.c' measured is unmodified; the wrapper TU used for the gc-sections cross-check and the driver #include the file rather than patch it. (7) A prior partial run left files in this directory; BUILD.txt, driver.c (raw-mode + unfinished-capture fix added), classify.py and all numbers above were regenerated in this run (hostcore/ objects; the old hostlib/ dir was removed).
